headline: BTC breaks below the true market mean as $356M is liquidated and the Coinbase premium hits a record low; ETFs still took in $424M over three days.
summary: The close fell below the $79,631 true market mean, putting roughly 1.32M BTC of new coins bought at $80–82K underwater; the next line is the $75,800 short-term holder cost basis, 2.6% below. Leveraged longs were flushed and weighted funding fell from 10.00% to 0.64% in a day, yet the Coinbase premium of −0.271% is the lowest on our record: US spot is selling and ETF inflows did not absorb it. Bull day 21, no exit rule fired; watch whether STH-SOPR drops below 0.99.

news.title: BTC drops below $80,000; $356M of futures liquidated in 24 hours, $205M of it longs
news.read: Liquidations amplified the drop: our weighted funding fell from 10.00% to 0.64% in a day and Hyperliquid flipped negative, so a large share of leveraged longs was cleared. This is a short-term structural change and does not affect the market stage. Price later closed at $77,800, below the $79,800 in the article; the evening liquidations (TokenPost counted at least $659M by 17:15 ET) are not in this figure.

news.title: Alphabet misses on earnings and closes down nearly 13%, Nasdaq −1.4%; the 10-year yield falls 11.3bp to 4.938%
news.read: The tech retreat pulled BTC down with it (our 30-day correlation with the Nasdaq is 0.62, FRED Oct 28). Lower yields are normally supportive, but risk aversion dominated on the day. This is short-term risk sentiment and does not affect the cycle call; what matters is whether US spot (Coinbase premium −0.271%) keeps selling.

news.title: US Q3 GDP advance estimate +3.4% annualized (Q2 2.2%); Q3 core PCE prices +2.5% annualized
news.read: Strong growth and cooler quarterly prices; September PCE (+0.5% m/m, core +3.1% y/y, per Yahoo Finance) matched expectations, giving no new reason for a December hike and not removing one either. A neutral backdrop for BTC; the 2.67% real yield (FRED Oct 28) remains a high-level headwind and does not affect the cycle call.

news.title: US spot BTC ETFs take in $137.3M on Oct 28, a third straight day of inflows, $136M of it into IBIT
news.read: This is the day before the drop; we list it as a provisional value (Farside matches at $137.3M). Three days total $424M, almost all IBIT, which contradicts the record-low Coinbase premium: ETFs are buying while spot on Coinbase is selling. ETF inflows are flows backdrop only; the Oct 29 flow on the down day is what to watch.

news.title: Binance wallet movements spark hack rumors as BTC slides from $80,800 toward $78,000 (unverified)
news.read: The article itself says the on-chain alerts did not confirm a breach, and no Binance response was reported. We do not treat it as fact and only note that it coincided with the evening drop. Exchange supply (Oct 28, 7-day +0.31%) does not yet cover Oct 29; next issue will show whether there were unusual outflows.

news.title: Strategy reports $19.53B Q3 net income on BTC fair-value gains and holds 848,517 BTC; preferreds move to daily dividends, CFO leaves Nov 5
news.read: The profit is a mark-to-market revaluation, not new buying; daily dividends make the preferreds more cash-like and keep the funding channel for BTC purchases open. Shares fell 3.5% after hours. No effect on the cycle call; our flows read still rests on ETFs and the Coinbase premium.

news.title: Coinbase Q3 total revenue $1.216B, down 35% y/y; transaction revenue down 44%; net income $719M
news.read: Retail trading is much thinner than a year ago, consistent with a persistently negative Coinbase premium (30-day average −0.104%): US retail spot demand has not come back. Industry backdrop; it does not affect the cycle call.

findings.title: Below the true market mean, $80–82K new coins go underwater; $76K cost is next
findings.lean_why: The thickest layer of new buyers went from profit to unrealized loss in a single day, supply is thin down to $66K, and price is only 2.6% above the cost-basis line; but we have not yet seen them realize losses.
findings.what: Question: after the break below the true market mean, who is underwater and where is the next line? Oct 29 closed at $77,800 (−4.29%), below the $79,631 true market mean (bitcoin-data Oct 23, −2.3%) and only +2.6% above the $75,800 short-term holder cost basis (bitcoin-data Oct 23); volume was 1.85× the 20-day average and the close sat at 2.7% of the day's range.
findings.why: Participants (CheckOnChain actual coin age, data date Oct 28): short-term holders 3.637M BTC at an average cost of $75,142; the two thickest buckets, $80K (743K BTC) and $82K (578K BTC), total about 1.32M BTC and are now above the close, i.e. in unrealized loss. Two points in time (modeled, Sep 20 → Oct 28): the 1.476M BTC bought since and not yet moved sit mainly in the $80K (715K), $82K (416K) and $84K (254K) buckets, exactly the buyers who took over above $80K. Cost map: about $215M of bids at $77,000 and $55M at $75,000 (mostly Hyperliquid perps, 00:06 UTC); the Oct 30 expiry holds 32.7% of OI with max pain at $78,000. Behavior check: Oct 28 STH-SOPR 1.0029 and short-term realized loss of 1,975 BTC were measured at $81K; down-day behavior arrives next issue. The contradiction: ETFs still took in $137.3M on Oct 28 (provisional), yet the Coinbase premium of −0.271% is our record low.
findings.alt: The break is one day old, and the true market mean is bitcoin-data's Oct 23 value (about 7 days late); Glassnode's indicator of the same name is $77.9K (different methodology), on which today merely touches it. Unrealized loss does not mean selling: the three loss-taking lows in Jul–Aug were all shallow (STH-SOPR low 0.9762), and new buyers may choose to hold. Modeled STH total differs from actual by −2.0%, with 9.9% misplaced; per-UTXO, not entity-adjusted, so not compared in size with Glassnode figures.
findings.history: The brief has no historical sample of 'first break below the true market mean after a bull call'; bitcoin-data's last short-term-cost cross below the true market mean was 2026-04-27. The last three STH-SOPR loss lows (Jul 13 0.9762, Aug 1 0.9936, Aug 14 0.9946) were all near $62K; 3 samples, background only.
findings.so: Scenarios (conditional, CheckOnChain Oct 28): at a $76,000 close about 2.29M short-term BTC would be underwater (63%), at $74,000 about 2.32M, at $66,000 about 2.46M; from $76K down to $66K adds only 170K BTC (thin supply), and $64,000 jumps to 2.89M. Logic chain: the $80–82K support layer has been lost, so last issue's 'new buyers defend their cost' no longer holds; loss-taking has not appeared and price is still above the short-term cost, so 'short-term capitulation' does not hold yet either. Market stage and exit framework are unchanged; the gap to the 200-day MA narrowed to 6.0%.
findings.next: By Nov 5: a close back above the $79,631 true market mean would mark this as a one-day shakeout and refute the call; STH-SOPR below 0.99 (deeper than the Aug 1 and Aug 14 lows) would show underwater new buyers starting to realize losses, confirming that selling pressure has turned.

findings.title: Leverage flushed, but US spot is selling: Coinbase premium at a record low
findings.lean_why: Clearing leverage would normally ease selling pressure, but US spot keeps selling at a discount on Coinbase and ETF inflows did not absorb it, so demand remains weak.
findings.what: Coinbase premium daily value −0.271% (Oct 29), our percentile 0 (n=299); 7-day average −0.159%, 1-year percentile 0.3 and the lowest in 121 days (last 2026-06-30, −0.161). The same day weighted funding fell from 10.00% to 0.64%, and CoinDesk counted $356M liquidated in 24 hours, $205M of it longs.
findings.why: Decomposition: who moved price? Derivatives: Hyperliquid funding flipped from 10.95% to −8.54% (the largest venue by OI, $3.47B), OKX stays at 10.95% and Deribit is back to 7.54%; liquidations were mostly longs, so leverage was flushed. Spot: the Coinbase discount to Binance widened, so US spot sellers were more urgent. Cross-check: ETFs +$424M over Oct 26–28 (Oct 28 provisional), only in IBIT, point the opposite way from the Coinbase discount; stablecoin supply −1.17% over 7 days and −$6.2B over 30 days (DefiLlama Oct 29), so no fresh money is coming in. Options: 30-day risk reversal −3.04 → −4.94 and DVOL 37.26 → 41.99, downside protection is pricier again.
findings.alt: The Coinbase premium is a daily-close ratio and a single day can be skewed by large trades in US hours; ETF creations often execute on Coinbase Prime, so the premium and ETF flows need not move together. Liquidation totals differ by tracker (CoinDesk $356M; TokenPost at least $659M by 17:15 ET, different windows). Funding is a spot reading and swings within a day.
findings.history: Signal history: the 7-day average has hit a 1-year 2% extreme only twice (after 2026-06-02 the next 30 days were −7.7%; after 2026-06-28, +7.1%); too few samples, background only; median −0.3% vs a same-period baseline of +3.5%.
findings.so: What changed is the read on who is buying: last issue treated the ETF return as a better spot picture, but today only IBIT is buying while Coinbase and stablecoins are flowing out. What did not change: leveraged longs have been largely cleared, so the room for liquidations to amplify the next drop is smaller. Market stage and exit framework are unchanged.
findings.next: By Nov 5: a Coinbase premium 7-day average back above −0.05% would show US spot selling fading and refute the call; a 7-day average below −0.2% would show spot selling still widening and confirm it.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Quiet Under $85K
items.points: $84–85K has capped price four times this year; US spot ETF cost basis $81.5K, true market mean $77.9K, short-term holder cost basis $75.8K; about $42M of bids at $78–79K; 1-month realized volatility near 25%, close to summer 2023; conclusion: range-bound, thin demand but light selling.
items.meaning: Today's $77,800 close is below its $81.5K ETF cost basis and near its $77.9K true market mean; our bitcoin-data true market mean is $79,631 (different methodology), and we keep our own series and call it a break. 'Light selling' was challenged by today's −4.29% high-volume drop; the Oct 29 loss-taking data is needed to judge.
